theme: 3 terms on generics in depth: conforming only sometimes, filling in a protocol's type with brackets, and taking any number of types

terms.definition: A way for a generic type to conform to a protocol only when its type parameter also conforms.
terms.example: Thanks to Conditional Conformance, an array of `Int` is Equatable.

terms.definition: An associated type you can fill in with angle brackets after a protocol name, like `Collection<Int>`.
terms.example: With a Primary Associated Type, we can write `some Collection<Int>`.

terms.definition: A generic feature, written with `each` and `repeat`, that lets a function take any number of values of different types.
terms.example: A Parameter Pack lets `log` take an `Int`, a `String` and a `Bool` at once.

quizzes.question: What lets a function take any number of values of different types?
In this code, what do you call making `Box` Equatable only when `T` is Equatable?
What do you call the type you fill in after a protocol name, as in `Collection<Int>`?

video.description:
Learn to explain advanced generics in Swift: Conditional Conformance, Primary Associated Type & Parameter Pack, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Conditional Conformance - A way for a generic type to conform to a protocol only when its type parameter also conforms.
Primary Associated Type - An associated type you can fill in with angle brackets after a protocol name, like `Collection<Int>`.
Parameter Pack - A generic feature, written with `each` and `repeat`, that lets a function take any number of values of different types.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.description:
Explain Conditional Conformance, Primary Associated Type & Parameter Pack in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
조건부 준수, 기본 연관 타입, 파라미터 팩 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Conditional Conformance - A way for a generic type to conform to a protocol only when its type parameter also conforms.
한국어: 조건부 준수: 제네릭 타입이 타입 파라미터도 준수할 때만 프로토콜을 준수하게 하는 방법

Primary Associated Type - An associated type you can fill in with angle brackets after a protocol name, like `Collection<Int>`.
한국어: 기본 연관 타입: Collection<Int>처럼 프로토콜 이름 뒤 꺾쇠괄호로 채울 수 있는 연관 타입

Parameter Pack - A generic feature, written with `each` and `repeat`, that lets a function take any number of values of different types.
한국어: 파라미터 팩: each와 repeat로 쓰며, 서로 다른 타입의 값을 개수 제한 없이 받게 해 주는 제네릭 기능

In this video, Mina and Jake sort out why a generic box can be compared, what brackets on a protocol mean and how one function takes any mix of values, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

dialogue.title: Brackets on a protocol?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, why can I compare two `Box` values here?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Look at the extension. It's a Conditional Conformance.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So `Box` is Equatable only when `T` is Equatable?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. With Conditional Conformance, a box of a non-Equatable type can't be compared.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And `Collection<Int>` in `sum`? Brackets on a protocol?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's a Primary Associated Type. It says the elements must be `Int`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So arrays and sets both work, if they hold `Int`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. The Primary Associated Type keeps `sum` short.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's a Parameter Pack. `log` takes any number of values, of any types.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Conditional Conformance, Primary Associated Type and a Parameter Pack. Generics in depth!
Conditional Conformance: Equatable only when the inside is.
